runtime.name: omp
runtime.configuration: Conflicting-writers fixture plus generated poteto-mode/feature Skills and native implementer role; cursor/default; task isolation was described in the prompt but not enabled in the actual task schema.
runtime.permissionProfile: root and two writable implementers shared one disposable checkout

assertions.evidence: The run used the repository-generated router, feature workflow, and implementer role.
Poteto-mode selected feature for the intentional settings change.
The root named the blocking same-file gate, disjoint semantic work, shared mutable file, and intended isolated strategy.
The four required hashes were captured before the task call.
The root declared isolation, but the actual task call contained neither isolated:true nor any other active isolation control.
Exactly BatchWriter and RetryWriter were started.
Assignments were disjoint, but both children observed and rewrote the shared file while the other was active.
Both writers ran concurrently in the same checkout; neither real isolation nor serialization protected the shared mutation.
The writers exchanged acknowledgements and repaired each other's observed changes instead of producing independent frozen results.
The root observed the race only after the shared checkout had lost RetryWriter's change.
Only maxBatch=25 remained in the root checkout; delayMs had reverted to 100.
External node verify.mjs combined failed because delayMs was 100 rather than 250.
The root did not select the serialized fallback after discovering that isolation controls were absent.
The race was confined to workspace/settings.mjs.
No commit, push, publication, or pull request occurred.

limitations: The run was interrupted after the writer-to-writer acknowledgement loop and failed combined verification were established.
The hardened fixture now requires observable isolation metadata, forbids horizontal writer communication, and mandates serialization when isolation cannot be observed.
